_comments: JournalEntryBatch · AfterUpdate — ERP handoff confirmation / exception alerting.
plans/mj-entity-action-workflow-adoption.md §3, row 3.
WHY AfterUpdate AND NOT BeforeUpdate/Validate: the batch lock trigger (error 50009) and the
balanced-JE constraint trigger are DEFERRABLE constraint triggers that fire at COMMIT. A
Before*/Validate binding runs INSIDE that same transaction and would be interleaved with them.
After* is dispatched outside it, so an alert can never deadlock or roll back a dispatch.
THIS BINDING MUST NEVER WRITE TO THE BATCH. Once Status is Approved/Sent/Posted the batch lock
trigger allows only Status / ApprovedAt / ApprovedByUserID / SentAt / PostedAt /
ExternalJournalEntryBatchRef / ErrorMessage to change (error 50009); CompanyID, PostingDate,
SummaryJournalEntryID and the approval-task pointer freeze at approval. A binding that tried
would surface a raw trigger error from inside an action run, which is why it only reads.
After* is fire-and-forget — NOT part of any all-or-none transaction. Nothing about the ledger
may depend on this having run. It is an alert, not a step in the dispatch.
SHIPPED AS Pending, NOT Active. GenericDatabaseProvider dispatches only bindings whose
EntityAction.Status AND EntityActionInvocation.Status are both 'Active', so a Pending row is
inert. It is Pending for two reasons, both of which an administrator must resolve first:
1. NO TRANSITION FILTER EXISTS YET. The adoption doc assumed MJ#3408 seeded reusable
'field changed' / 'field changed to value' ActionFilters. It did NOT — that is plan text in
MJ's plans/entity-action-workflow-extensions.md only, and MJ's ActionFilter table has no
Name column, so such a row is not even expressible as a reusable lookup. The real
mechanism landed later (MJ commit df76df876d, 2026-08-08) as a filter row GENERATED per
trigger, whose Code embeds the field and value as literal arguments:
DidFieldChangeToValue('Status', 'Sent')
against an ActionFilterContext the installed @memberjunction/actions-base@6.1.0-edge.1
does NOT ship (no EntityChangeContext.js in its dist). Until that engine lands, AfterUpdate
fires on EVERY save of a batch, not just the Pending→Sent transition — which is exactly the
re-firing failure the doc warns about. Do not set this Active before then.
2. To / From / Provider are deployment configuration, not app metadata. They are deliberately
absent below rather than filled with placeholders that would look configured.
SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY UNSET. The doc calls for scoping to a Company, but ScopeRecordID must be a
concrete Company UUID and CK_EntityAction_Scope requires ScopeEntityID and ScopeRecordID to be
both NULL or both set — so a specific company cannot be seeded by an app repo that ships to many
tenants. Unset means 'applies to every batch', which is correct for a Pending template.
To narrow it, set ScopeEntityID to the MJ: Companies entity and ScopeRecordID to the company's
bare UUID (NOT MJ's 'ID|<guid>' CompositeKey form — the resolver compares String(fieldValue)).
Scoping is verified to work for this entity: EntityActionScopeResolver's default FK walk needs
EXACTLY ONE field on the subject entity pointing at MJ: Companies, and JournalEntryBatch has
exactly one (CompanyID). Zero or two or more would make the binding silently never fire.

fields.Value:
const b = EntityActionContext.entityObject;
return `Journal entry batch ${b.JournalEntryBatchNumber} is now ${b.Status} (${b.TargetSystem})`;

_comments: JournalEntry · AfterCreate — threshold alerting on large or manual entries.
plans/mj-entity-action-workflow-adoption.md §3, row 4.
AfterCreate is the only defensible invocation here. A JE is written together with its lines and
the debits=credits invariant is a DEFERRABLE constraint trigger checked at COMMIT, so at
BeforeCreate/Validate time the entry is not yet balanced and any binding that inspected it would
be reading a half-built entry. After* runs once the entry is real and committed.
THIS BINDING MUST NEVER WRITE TO THE ENTRY. Once Status ∈ {Batched, GLPosted} the JE immutability
trigger allows only GLPostedAt / GLReferenceID / Status to change. It only reads.
After* is fire-and-forget — never make the ledger depend on it having run.
SHIPPED AS Pending. Two gaps an administrator must close first:
1. NO THRESHOLD IS EXPRESSED, so as written this alerts on EVERY journal entry created, which
is not what anyone wants in production. Two things are missing. First, the transition/
predicate ActionFilter mechanism is not in the installed engine (see the batch binding above).
Second — and this is a schema fact, not an engine gap — the JournalEntry HEADER CARRIES NO
AMOUNT. Debits and credits live on JournalEntryLine, so 'unusually large' cannot be decided
from the record this binding receives. A real threshold has to sum the Lines collection,
which is work for a purpose-built Action, not for a Script param.
'Manual' entries ARE decidable from the header: EntryType = 'Manual'.
2. To / From / Provider are deployment configuration and are deliberately left unset.
SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY UNSET, for the same reason as the batch binding. JournalEntry likewise has
exactly one FK to MJ: Companies (CompanyID), so the default FK-walk scope resolution will work
once an administrator sets ScopeEntityID + ScopeRecordID together.

fields.Value:
const je = EntityActionContext.entityObject;
return `Journal entry ${je.EntryNumber} created (${je.EntryType})`;
